sections.text: Each shared datastore, the one that reaches 90% first on top: its used % now, its runway and how it moved since last month. The first 10 of 13; the workbook has all (vm_capacity_top_datastores).
sections.title: Runway: datastores

sections.text: The used % behind each line: 90, 60 and 30 days ago and now (the sample nearest each day).
sections.title: The numbers behind the lines

rows: room for about 52 more average VMs
sections.text: All 3 cluster(s) of vCenter vc01 together: 12 hosts (12 usable), 120 VMs powered on. "After host failure" and "N-1" are the use with 1 host(s) of each cluster down (the cluster must still run everything): the CPU and memory runways run to 80% / 80% of what is left then, not to 100% of what is installed. Growth is fitted on vCenter's daily statistics of the last 90 days.
sections.title: Overall

sections.text: Per cluster: hosts usable (connected, not in maintenance), CPU and memory used now, memory used if the biggest 1 host(s) fail (the cluster must still run everything: amber from 80%, red at 100%), vCPUs per physical core (amber from 4.0), VMs powered on and their average size, memory growth, the memory runway (days until memory after a host failure reaches 80% - "80% N-1" - not until the hosts are full), how many more VMs of the average size fit (and what limits them), how many hosts of the cluster's average size are recommended to keep memory and CPU at 80% / 80% with a host down (now, and at the current growth within 12 months), and VMs added / removed in the last 30 days.
sections.title: Clusters: CPU and memory

sections.text: Per cluster, its shared datastores together: capacity, free, used %, provisioned % (thin disks counted at their full size: over 100% means overcommitted), growth, and the days until 85% and until full at that growth.
sections.title: Clusters: storage

sections.text: Each shared datastore, the ones that reach 90% first on top: growth fitted on vCenter's daily used space, the days (and date) until 85%, 90% and full, and how well a straight line fits the history (poor = jumps: snapshots deleted, VMs moved - the runway is a rough guide then).
sections.title: Datastores: runway

sections.text: Every host: state (Low: in maintenance, red: not connected - neither counts as capacity), cores, CPU and memory used now, VMs. Hosts much fuller than their neighbours mean DRS is off or limited.
